Archibald McDonald of Keppoch

My transcription of this scottish slow air from John Cunningham. I have it in the album “25 Years of Celtic Music”.
6th bar is played like |f3ga2| the first time only.

↳ Posted by PJ Mediterranean on March 24th, 2007.

That would be the 5th bar actually. The pickup doesn’t count as a bar. :) Nice tune though. I’ll go over it later when I get some time.

↳ Posted by Jeffery on March 24th, 2007.

Archie MacDonald of Keppoch

This lovely tune has been played at all our family gatherings! Hope others love playing it as much as i do ! (it sounds great on Clarsach! )

↳ Posted by davesim on March 24th, 2007.

Mmm… I actually meant the 6th bar though. I didn’t explain it very well, I meant the 6th bar that is |f3ed2| is played by John Cunningham like |f3ga2| the first time, when he starts the tune, but not anymore.
And I agree with Davesim this tune is lovely.

Re: Archibald McDonald Of Keppoch

Traditional Tune Archive shows this air in 6/8.
“The tune was first published by the Scots fiddler, collector and composer Captain Simon Fraser (1773-1852) of Ardachie, near Fort Augustus. Fraser’s work, The Airs and Melodies Peculiar to the Highlands of Scotland and the Isles (1816), contained many works collected from various sources during the period 1715-1745.”
https://tunearch.org/wiki/Annotation:Archibald_MacDonald_of_Keppoch

Performed by Alasdair Fraser & Natalie Haas:
https://youtu.be/gnzSikQVcOw

David ‘Daggar’ Gordon plays this in a set with ‘The Kail Pot’ (https://thesession.org/tunes/9770) & his ‘The Lambing Storm’ (https://thesession.org/tunes/5672) - on Gordon’s ‘Highland Mandolin’ album (1988).

Re: Archibald McDonald Of Keppoch

Has anyone been able to find the original Simon Fraser publication? I looked in both the 1816 and 1874 editions of “The Airs and Melodies Peculiar to the Highlands of Scotland and the Isles” but didn’t find this tune in either of them.

↳ Posted by Sean McLeod on October 9th, 2025.

Re: Archibald McDonald Of Keppoch

I don’t think it’s in either of the editions of Simon Fraser, Sean, nor is it in “Airs & Melodies” Volume 2 [1]. It’s not even in The Scottish Fiddle Music Index (Gore 1994). The earliest published version I’ve got is from 1997 in a collection by Scots fiddler Ron Gonnella; he says “collected by Capt Simon Fraser,” but no further information. It’s a mystery.

[1] = Lost for almost a hundred years, it was found in a second-hand bookshop in 1952 by Professor Sydney Newman of Edinburgh University.

↳ Posted by Nigel Gatherer on October 10th, 2025.

Re: Archibald McDonald Of Keppoch

There is an earlier published version from 1988 by Christine Martin in her Ceol na Fidhle series of books. The Traditional Tune Archive also says Archibald MacDonald of Keppoch is in Alan Lerwick’s Kilted Fiddler (1985).

Interestingly, although the TTA says “first published by … Captain Simon Fraser”, it doesn’t specifically say in what publication it appeared, although it then goes on to mention the 1816 collection.

Archibald McDonald Of Keppoch, X:6

This is my best attempt to transcribe the Simon/Angus Fraser version of the tune which can be found in the Angus Fraser Manuscript in the University of Edinburgh Heritage Collections, as Coll-58, or MS614. I have blogged in more detail about how and why I found the tune at https://patterncastle.com/. Note that the tune in the manuscript is in 6/8 time rather than 3/4.

↳ Posted by cicelyp on November 25th, 2025.
